nodes.label: Menu Action Panel
nodes.rationale: Cream card with hard pixel border groups all navigation in one bottom-anchored block, keeping controls within thumb reach on a portrait mobile layout.

nodes.label: Philippine Eagle Mascot
nodes.rationale: The Philippine eagle (national bird) is used as a culturally grounded guide character, standing in for a generic mascot so the game reads as distinctly Filipino.

nodes.label: Filipino-Language Interface Copy
nodes.rationale: Narrative copy is in Filipino while navigation labels stay in English, matching bilingual Filipino student habits and keeping button affordances unambiguous.

nodes.label: JOIN Button
nodes.rationale: Full-width green button with thick outline and dark offset shadow is the highest-contrast element, following classic game 'press start' primacy on the title screen.

nodes.label: Night Sky Background with Stars and Clouds
nodes.norm_label: night sky background with stars and clouds
nodes.rationale: Deep blue gradient with scattered star pixels and a silhouetted cloud bank frames the mascot and creates calm, storybook atmosphere; high contrast keeps yellow title and green button legible.

nodes.label: Pixel Art Visual Style
nodes.rationale: Low-resolution sprite art, chunky borders and hard drop shadows are applied consistently to logo, mascot and every control so UI chrome never breaks the retro illusion.

nodes.label: Top-Right Settings Icon Button
nodes.rationale: A single small square icon in the corner (gear-like mark) holds secondary/global options, keeping the main menu uncluttered.

nodes.label: Student Role Button
nodes.rationale: Dark, de-emphasized plaque shows the currently selected role; its visual weight below the mascot suggests role switching exists but is not the primary action on this screen.

nodes.label: Tagline Prompt "Ang pagkakamali ay bahagi ng pagkakatuo"
nodes.norm_label: tagline prompt "ang pagkakamali ay bahagi ng pagkakatuo"
nodes.rationale: Framed like a dialogue box with a downward pointer, mimicking retro RPG NPC speech to deliver an encouraging, mistake-friendly message before the quiz begins (reduces quiz anxiety).

nodes.label: Fili Quiz Mo Title Logo
nodes.rationale: Yellow pixel-block lettering with a drop shadow plus a small sun glyph (echoing the Philippine flag sun) establishes Filipino identity and an 8-bit retro game tone immediately on first load.

nodes.label: Fili Quiz Mo Home Screen
nodes.rationale: Landing screen of a Filipino-language quiz game; a single dominant JOIN call-to-action with only two low-emphasis secondary actions reduces decision friction for students entering a quiz session.

nodes.rationale: This Next.js release has breaking changes in APIs, conventions and file structure, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs guides before writing code and heed deprecation notices instead of relying on trained knowledge.

nodes.label: AI-Powered Filipino Quiz Generator
nodes.rationale: Quizzes are generated from phone-camera input by a trained AI model so teachers can create DepEd-aligned Grade 6 Filipino quizzes within a minute while students practice gamified Tagalog grammar items.

nodes.label: Admin TOTP multi-factor authentication (AAL2)
nodes.rationale: Admins enroll an authenticator on first password sign-in and must supply a current TOTP code afterwards; admin dashboard access additionally requires AAL2 so a stolen password alone is insufficient.

nodes.label: Trusted app_metadata.role authorization
nodes.rationale: Roles must live in trusted app_metadata (set only by a trusted administrator or server process) because user_metadata is user-editable and therefore unusable for authorization.

nodes.label: Row Level Security policy enforcement
nodes.rationale: Database policies validate trusted admin metadata and auth.jwt()->>'aal' = 'aal2' because route protection does not replace database authorization.

nodes.label: Supabase Authentication Setup
nodes.rationale: Separate admin and teacher Supabase roles are enforced with server-side checks plus database policies, rather than relying on client routing or a cookie-refresh proxy.

nodes.label: Server routes as authorization boundary
nodes.rationale: /admin-dashboard independently verifies user, admin role and AAL2, and /teacher-dashboard verifies user and teacher role; the proxy only refreshes Supabase cookies and is explicitly not the authorization boundary.

nodes.label: Webpack production build choice
nodes.rationale: The project builds with Webpack because Turbopack native bindings are unavailable in the current Windows environment.

nodes.label: Albanya Dark Forest Question Text
nodes.rationale: Question text is a Filipino literary-comprehension claim about the dark forest outside Albanya where the story begins, indicating the quiz bank is drawn from Philippine literature (Florante at Laura) rather than generic trivia.

nodes.label: FALSE Answer Button
nodes.rationale: Orange fill with an X glyph, visually contrasted against the blue TRUE button so the binary choice is distinguishable at a glance without relying on reading.

nodes.label: Filipino Language Localization
nodes.rationale: All prompts and labels are in Filipino except the TRUE/FALSE answer tokens, which are kept in English as fixed answer vocabulary so the binary choice stays unambiguous.

nodes.label: Instruction Text (Sagutin ng TRUE or FALSE lamang.)
nodes.norm_label: instruction text (sagutin ng true or false lamang.)

nodes.label: NEXT Button
nodes.rationale: Green bottom-anchored action bar separated from the answer pair, so advancing to the next item is a distinct, deliberate step rather than an accidental tap next to an answer.

nodes.label: Pixel-Art Retro Visual Style
nodes.rationale: Chunky borders, monospace pixel font, hard drop shadows and a low-resolution city skyline strip deliberately mimic an 8-bit arcade game, likely to make an educational assessment feel playful and less test-like for students.

nodes.label: Question Progress Segments
nodes.rationale: Ten discrete segments (one filled yellow) instead of a continuous bar: the blocky meter matches the pixel-art language and makes the 10-question set countable.

nodes.label: Question Card (TANONG 1)
nodes.rationale: Cream paper-like panel with a gold header band and blue dotted divider; isolates the question from the answer buttons so the learner reads before acting, and the bold 'TANONG 1' header gives an arcade-style sense of progression.

nodes.label: Timer and Score HUD
nodes.rationale: Clock icon with a red draining bar plus an 'S' score badge sit in the top-right: time pressure and scoring are surfaced continuously so performance is visible during, not only after, the quiz.

nodes.label: TRUE Answer Button
nodes.rationale: Blue fill with a check-mark glyph: blue/check reads as the affirmative, 'correct-leaning' choice, and the oversized full-width target maximizes tap accuracy on a phone.

nodes.label: True or False Quiz Screen
nodes.rationale: Full-screen mobile quiz mode presented as a retro pixel-art game: a compact HUD at the top, one question card in the center, two large answer buttons, and a persistent NEXT control pinned to the bottom so the primary action stays thumb-reachable.

nodes.label: Warm Earth-Tone Palette (Cream, Tan, Brown, Charcoal)
nodes.norm_label: warm earth-tone palette (cream, tan, brown, charcoal)

nodes.label: Navy and Sky Blue Palette with Primary Accents
nodes.norm_label: navy and sky blue palette with primary accents

nodes.label: Answer Choice Buttons
nodes.rationale: Four tappable word options (makamandag, malinis, mabilis, malalim) provide a recognition-based assist path and reduce typing friction on mobile; all are adjectives so the learner must judge meaning against the sentence context.

nodes.label: Your Answer Text Input
nodes.rationale: A free-text field with placeholder 'Type your answer...' lets learners produce the word themselves instead of only recognizing it, which tests recall rather than recognition.

nodes.label: Clear Button
nodes.rationale: A dedicated reset control lets players undo a mistaken typed or tapped answer without leaving the question.

nodes.label: Close Quiz Button
nodes.rationale: A persistent exit control gives an escape hatch from a timed quiz while keeping destructive navigation visually distinct (pink X on green) from forward actions.
nodes.source_location: top left HUD, green square with pink X

nodes.label: Countdown Timer
nodes.rationale: A visible per-question timer with a draining red bar adds game-like time pressure and discourages idle lookups.
nodes.source_location: top HUD, clock icon with red bar and '7'

nodes.label: Filipino Language Localization
nodes.rationale: Every label (Punan ang blangko, Tanong, Kumpletuhin ang pangungusap, Your answer, Choices, Clear) and the reading passage are in Filipino/Taglish, situating the quiz in a Philippine literature context.
nodes.source_location: all on-screen labels and question text

nodes.label: Next Button
nodes.rationale: A full-width, high-saturation green bar is the single obvious forward action, keeping the primary progression tap target large and thumb-reachable.

nodes.label: Retro Pixel-Art UI Style
nodes.rationale: Chunky dark outlines, pixel fonts, beveled cream panels and an 8-bit skyline evoke nostalgic handheld RPGs, making a school quiz feel like a game and increasing engagement for student players.

nodes.label: Pixel Skyline Background
nodes.rationale: A light-blue sky, pixel clouds and a silhouetted city over water provide themed scenery without competing with the question card for attention.
nodes.source_location: lower half of the screen behind the controls

nodes.label: Punan ang Blangko Mode
nodes.rationale: Naming the game mode in Filipino keeps the entire experience monolingual and immediately signals the task type (fill in the blank) before the question is read.
nodes.source_location: top HUD label, left of 1/5 counter

nodes.label: Question Progress 1 of 5
nodes.rationale: Dual progress readout (segment pips plus a numeric 1/5) tells the player both how far along they are and how much remains, supporting session-length expectations.
nodes.source_location: top HUD, five segment bar and '1/5'

nodes.label: Tanong Question Card
nodes.rationale: A high-contrast cream card with a bold yellow 'TANONG 1' banner isolates the prompt from the rest of the screen so the sentence being completed is the visual focus; the blank is rendered as a long underscore to invite completion.
nodes.source_location: yellow banner and cream card, upper middle

nodes.label: Fill in the Blanks Quiz Screen
nodes.norm_label: fill in the blanks quiz screen
nodes.rationale: Full-screen mobile quiz UI captured as a promotional/asset screenshot; retro pixel-art game framing turns a language quiz into a playful game loop rather than a plain form.
